source.title: A General Framework for Coloring Problems: Old Results, New Results, and Open Problems

accepted.question_text: For a planar graph G with maximum degree Delta, let chi_2(G) be the minimum number of colors needed for a vertex coloring in which every pair of vertices at graph distance one or two receives different colors. Is Wegner's bound true: chi_2(G) <= Delta + 5 for 4 <= Delta <= 7, and chi_2(G) <= floor(3Delta/2) + 1 for Delta >= 8?

evidence.quote: A distant-2-coloring of G is a coloring of the vertices such that vertices at distance one or two have different colors.
Conjecture 1. If G is a planar graph with maximum degree Delta, then chi2(G) <= Delta+5 for 4 <= Delta <= 7, and <= floor(3Delta/2)+1 for Delta >= 8.

accepted.question_text: For graphs of treewidth 2, what is the computational complexity of the radio coloring problem RC, where a radio coloring assigns positive integers to vertices so that adjacent vertices get labels differing by at least 2 and vertices at distance 2 get distinct labels, and the goal is to minimize the span, meaning the largest assigned label?

evidence.quote: The complexity of RC even for graphs of treewidth 2 is a long standing open question.
Recently Golovach proved that RC is NP-hard for graphs of treewidth 2.

accepted.question_text: Let G be a t-degenerate graph on n vertices, meaning every subgraph of G has a vertex of degree at most t. Let L' be an injective pre-labeling of some subset of vertices by positive integers, and let M be the larger of n and the maximum preassigned label. Does every such pre-labeling extend to a radio labeling of all vertices of G with span at most M + 3t, where radio labeling means an injective vertex labeling by positive integers in which adjacent vertices have labels differing by at least 2?
accepted.context_brief: Pre-labeled radio labeling in t-degenerate graphs

evidence.quote: Conjecture 10. If G is a t-degenerate graph and L' is a pre-labeling of G, then there exists a radio labeling extending L' with span <= M + 3t.

accepted.question_text: For interval graphs, determine the computational complexity of each of the following radio labeling variants: RL, where all vertices must receive distinct positive-integer labels and adjacent vertices must differ by at least 2 while minimizing span; p-RL(l), where a fixed number l of vertices are pre-labeled and the labeling must extend those values; and p-RL(*), where the number of pre-labeled vertices is part of the input.
accepted.context_brief: Radio labeling variants on interval graphs

evidence.quote: The complexity of any of the variants of Radio Labeling (RL, p-RL(l) and p-RL(*)) for interval graphs are open problems.

accepted.question_text: For cographs, determine the computational complexity of p-RL(l), the radio labeling problem with a fixed number l of pre-labeled vertices, where the required output is a minimum-span radio labeling extending the given pre-labeling.

evidence.quote: another open problem concerns the computational complexity of p-RL(l) for cographs.

accepted.question_text: For bipartite graphs, determine the computational complexity of p-RL(*), the radio labeling problem where an arbitrary input subset of vertices is already assigned distinct positive labels and the task is to find a minimum-span radio labeling extending that pre-labeling.
accepted.context_brief: Arbitrary-prelabel radio labeling on bipartite graphs

evidence.quote: The complexity of p-RL(*) for bipartite graphs is open.

accepted.question_text: For planar graphs and for graphs of bounded treewidth, determine the computational complexity of p-RL(*), the radio labeling problem where an arbitrary number of vertices may be pre-labeled in the input and the goal is to extend the pre-labeling to a minimum-span radio labeling.
accepted.context_brief: Arbitrary-prelabel radio labeling on planar and bounded-treewidth graphs

evidence.quote: p-RL(l) is polynomial for planar graphs and graphs of bounded treewidth.
The complexity of p-RL(*) for these graph classes is open.

accepted.question_text: Let G be a triangle-free graph with chromatic number chi(G), and let T be a spanning tree of G used as a backbone. A backbone coloring is a proper vertex coloring of G in which endpoints of every edge of T receive colors that differ by at least 2, and bbc(G,T) is the smallest number of colors needed. Does there exist a universal small constant c such that bbc(G,T) <= chi(G) + c for every triangle-free graph G and every spanning tree T?

evidence.quote: Does there exist a small constant c such that bbc(G,T) <= chi(G)+c holds for all triangle-free graphs G?

accepted.question_text: Let G be a chordal graph with chromatic number chi(G), and let T be a spanning tree of G used as a backbone. Is there a universal constant c such that every such pair (G,T) has backbone coloring number bbc(G,T) <= chi(G) + c, where backbone coloring requires a proper coloring of G and a color difference of at least 2 on every edge of T?

evidence.quote: does bbc(G,T) <= chi(G)+c hold for any chordal graph G with spanning tree T?

accepted.question_text: For every planar graph G and every spanning tree T of G used as a backbone, is the backbone coloring number at most 6? Equivalently, can the known universal upper bound bbc(G,T) <= 7, obtained from the 4-Color Theorem and the general spanning-tree bound, always be improved by one?
accepted.context_brief: Planar backbone coloring with spanning-tree backbones

evidence.quote: bbc(G,T) <= 7 holds for any planar graph G with spanning tree T.

accepted.question_text: For every planar graph G with a perfect matching M used as a backbone, what is the best universal upper bound on the backbone coloring number bbc(G,M)? In particular, can the known bound bbc(G,M) <= 6 be improved, given that examples show it cannot be improved all the way to 4?
accepted.context_brief: Planar backbone coloring with perfect-matching backbones

evidence.quote: bbc(G,M) <= 6 holds for any planar graph G with perfect matching M.
this bound 6 is not best possible
